ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Figure below indicates a modular structure of the homodimer. Three positions are indicated on the model. Position A is the active site. Position B is a region known to have a large number of nonpolar residues. Position C is known to have a large number of charged residues. A mutation is discovered in the gene for ARKKKK60491 that converts a positively charged lysine residue into a negatively charged glutamic acid residue. This single change directly impacts the location where the substrate to ARKKKK60491 attaches during catalysis. Which position is likely affected by this change?
